speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I understand you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to help me identify the cause, please describe when these symptoms first started and how severe they are on a scale of 1 to 10.

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds exhausting; given your recent travel, hiking, camping, and multiple illnesses, have you noticed any specific patterns, such as muscle pain, fever, or issues with your legs that make you suspect something like Lyme disease or a tick-borne illness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The combination of progressive weakness, fatigue, and specifically mild diplopia (double vision) in a 33-year-old woman strongly suggests Myasthenia Gravis. Could you confirm if your double vision fluctuates throughout the day or worsens after physical activity?
